hints.title: Earliest arrival
hints.body: For each node you need the shortest travel time from `k`. The answer is the largest of those shortest times.

hints.title: Nonnegative weights
hints.body: All link times are nonnegative, so Dijkstra's algorithm applies even though the fastest route may use many links.

hints.title: Settle nodes in order
hints.body: Repeatedly settle the unsettled node with the smallest known distance and relax its outgoing links. With at most 100 nodes, a simple linear scan for the minimum is fast enough.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
dist[k] = 0, all other dist values = infinity
repeat until no reachable unsettled node remains:
    u = unsettled node with smallest dist
    mark u settled
    for each link (u, v, w):
        dist[v] = min(dist[v], dist[u] + w)
if any dist is infinity: return -1
return max(dist)
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete implementation.
